description:
## Reclassification

JMAP-x2gd.14 (P1) finds that `chat-server` carries 8 hand-maintained
`*_READONLY: &[&str]` lists keyed by wire-string name, each gated
by a `MAINTENANCE: when adding a server-set field to <Type> in
jmap-chat-types, add its wire name here too` comment. The
maintenance invariant is silently violable: a future field
addition that doesn't update the list lets clients overwrite a
server-set field, and tests don't fail.

A grep of `jmap-mail-server` (the canonical extension-server
template) confirms the same pattern with the same MAINTENANCE
contract:

- `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:661-663`: byte-equivalent
  `MAINTENANCE: This list must match all server-set fields of the
  Mailbox struct... If a new server-set field is added to Mailbox,
  add its wire name here. Drift...` comment.
- `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/identity.rs:323`: `const
  IDENTITY_READONLY: &[&str] = &["email", "id", "mayDelete"]`.

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" propagation rule,
fixing chat-server in isolation creates divergence from the
canonical. Whatever mechanism replaces the hand-maintained list
(trait method, proc-macro, serde-attribute) MUST land on
jmap-mail-server first then propagate.

## Scope of the workspace sweep

Two flavors of fix-site:

(A) **Per-server-crate READONLY lists**: 8 sites in chat-server,
plus mailbox.rs + identity.rs in mail-server, plus presumed
analogs in calendars-server / contacts-server / tasks-server /
filenode-server / metadata-server / sharing-server. Each
extension-server crate has its own pile of these.

(B) **The underlying types crates**: jmap-chat-types,
jmap-mail-types, jmap-calendars-types, etc. The mitigations
JMAP-x2gd.14 proposes (move the readonly list to a
`JmapObject`/`ReadOnlyFields` trait, or generate via a proc-macro
that lives in the types crate, or per-field `#[serde]` attributes
on the patch type) ALL require changes to the types crate, not
just the server crate.

## Mitigations from JMAP-x2gd.14

1. Move readonly list to a marker-trait method on each
   `JmapObject` — compiler enforces every type names its
   server-set fields once. Handler reads from the trait.
2. Derive readonly list from a struct attribute via a proc-macro
   in the types crate.
3. Tag fields with `#[serde(skip_deserializing)]` on the
   patch type (separate from the get type).

Each option has cross-extension implications. Option 1 is most
consistent with the workspace's hand-written-trait posture and
needs no new crates. Option 2 introduces a proc-macro dependency
which the workspace currently avoids. Option 3 requires every
type's patch-shape to be wholly separate from its get-shape,
which the workspace has not committed to.

## Precedent

This reclassification mirrors:
- **JMAP-x2gd.67** — 7 prior api-contract findings reclassified as
  workspace-canonical via mail-server cross-walk.
- **JMAP-x2gd.69** — JMAP-x2gd.64 reclassified.
- **JMAP-x2gd.86** — JMAP-x2gd.59 reclassified (foundation methods
  doc gap).

## What this bead does NOT decide

The mitigation choice (option 1 vs 2 vs 3) is workspace-architectural
and likely requires its own design discussion when the sweep is
worked. Adopting any of the three propagates across ~15 crates
(8 server crates + 8 types crates).

## Recommendation

When this sweep is worked:
1. Workspace-architectural discussion: pick option 1 vs 2 vs 3.
   File the decision as its own bead with the workspace-architecture
   label.
2. Audit every extension-server crate's `*_READONLY` lists.
3. Implement the chosen mitigation on the canonical pair
   (jmap-mail-types + jmap-mail-server) first.
4. Propagate to all 7 other type+server pairs in the same pass.
5. Close JMAP-x2gd.14 (and any analogous beads filed for the
   other siblings) when the propagation lands.

## Engineering basis

- chat-server: 8 `*_READONLY` sites (per JMAP-x2gd.14).
- mail-server: mailbox.rs:661-663 + identity.rs:323 (this bead).
- Workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" propagation rule.
- Precedent: JMAP-x2gd.67, JMAP-x2gd.69, JMAP-x2gd.86.
title: Workspace-canonical reclassification of JMAP-x2gd.14: per-type READONLY string lists are a workspace-wide maintainer-burden pattern
